# What Prefect API keys the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# The keys here are built from the ordered run
# 0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz, which no real credential is. That run is
# thirty-six characters and so is a whole key body — the shortest one the pattern
# reads, since the count is a floor. It is spelled in lowercase where the case
# does not matter and in uppercase where the case is what a case is about: base62
# holds the letters of both, so either spelling is a body.
#
# Four cases carry a key whose body is not that run, because what each of them
# turns on is a body the run cannot state. The two digest cases that reach a key
# are written in the sixteen hexadecimal characters repeated, which is what makes
# them digests; the two base64url cases close their key on a stretch of one
# repeated character, which is what puts the key inside a longer encoding. The
# digests that reach no key carry no body of a key to be built either way.

patterns: prefect-api-key

# The two kinds Prefect Cloud issues. Each is pn, one character naming the kind
# and an underscore, and behind that the same body, so what the character says is
# whether the key was issued to a person or to a service account and not what the
# key may reach.

case:     a user key
in:       pnu_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «prefect-api-key»

case:     a service account key
in:       pnb_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «prefect-api-key»

# The places a key is written.

case:     a key in an environment assignment
in:       PREFECT_API_KEY=pnu_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      PREFECT_API_KEY=«prefect-api-key»

case:     a key in the line prefect config view prints
in:       PREFECT_API_KEY='pnu_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz' (from profile)
out:      PREFECT_API_KEY='«prefect-api-key»' (from profile)

case:     a key in the authorization header a request to the api carries
in:       Authorization: Bearer pnu_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      Authorization: Bearer «prefect-api-key»

case:     a key on the command line that logs the cli in
in:       prefect cloud login --key pnu_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      prefect cloud login --key «prefect-api-key»

case:     a service account key in the environment a worker is given
in:       docker run -e PREFECT_API_KEY=pnb_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz prefecthq/prefect
out:      docker run -e PREFECT_API_KEY=«prefect-api-key» prefecthq/prefect

case:     a key in a profiles.toml entry
in:       [profiles.default]\nPREFECT_API_KEY = "pnb_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
out:      [profiles.default]\nPREFECT_API_KEY = "«prefect-api-key»"

# The alphabet the thirty-six characters are written in. Prefect names none, and
# base62 — the letters of both cases and the digits — is what the rules reading
# this format state and what the format's own shape asks for: the alphabet that
# adds the underscore to base62 is base64url, which adds the hyphen with it, and
# a body admitting the underscore would carry the character the prefix is read
# off by. Either of the two ends a body here, wherever in one it stands.

case:     a body written in capitals
in:       pnu_0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ
out:      «prefect-api-key»

case:     a body carrying a hyphen
in:       pnu_0123456789abcdef-ghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      pnu_0123456789abcdef-ghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz

case:     a body carrying an underscore
in:       pnu_0123456789abcdef_ghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      pnu_0123456789abcdef_ghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz

# The lengths either side of thirty-six, and what that number rests on — which
# differs between the two kinds. For a user key it is what the rules reading this
# format state, and Prefect's own troubleshooting page masks a key exactly that
# wide without writing a length down. For a service account key nothing states a
# body at all, and the same number is read there. Both are read as a floor rather
# than as a count: thirty-five characters are not a key, and thirty-seven are one
# key to the end of its run rather than a key and a character left over. What the
# floor costs is the middle case below, and it costs it for a service account key
# at any length under thirty-six.

case:     a body of thirty-six characters is a key
in:       pnb_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «prefect-api-key»

case:     a body of thirty-five characters is not
in:       pnb_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy
out:      pnb_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy

case:     an alphabet run longer than the floor is a key to the end of it
in:       pnu_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0
out:      «prefect-api-key»

case:     a service account key longer than the floor is a key to the end of it
in:       pnb_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123
out:      «prefect-api-key»

# What a key may be written against. The prefix is the whole of the anchor and
# there is no boundary on either side of it, so a key keeps its span whatever
# word character it abuts — and where the run of its alphabet carries on past the
# floor, what carries it on is redacted with the key. A hyphen and an underscore
# end the run instead.

case:     a key after an underscore
in:       PREFECT_API_KEY_pnu_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      PREFECT_API_KEY_«prefect-api-key»

case:     a key after a letter
in:       xpnu_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      x«prefect-api-key»

case:     a word written against a key
in:       pnu_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzsuffix
out:      «prefect-api-key»

case:     a hyphenated word written against a key
in:       pnu_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz-suffix
out:      «prefect-api-key»-suffix

case:     an underscored word written against a key
in:       pnu_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz_suffix
out:      «prefect-api-key»_suffix

case:     a key at the end of a sentence
in:       the key is pnu_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz.
out:      the key is «prefect-api-key».

# Two keys written together, which merge for two different reasons. The three
# characters in front of the underscore belong to the alphabet a body is written
# in, so a body may close with pn and a kind character and the underscore of the
# next key stand directly behind it; the second key then begins three characters
# before the first one ends, and the two spans overlap. Two keys written straight
# against each other merge as well, and the reason there is that a span reaches
# the end of its run: the first key's run carries on through the pn and the kind
# character of the second prefix and stops at that prefix's underscore, so the
# first span already covers where the second one begins. Parted by anything a run
# does not admit, they are two values and both go.

case:     a key beginning inside the key before it
in:       pnu_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwpnu_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «prefect-api-key»

case:     two keys with nothing between them
in:       pnu_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzpnb_0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ
out:      «prefect-api-key»

case:     two keys of different kinds separated by a space
in:       pnu_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz pnb_0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ
out:      «prefect-api-key» «prefect-api-key»

# What this pattern redacts that nobody issued. The prefix carries an underscore,
# which standard base64 writes nowhere, so only a base64url encoding can hold
# one. Where thirty-six base62 characters follow, the run from the prefix to the
# end of them is redacted whether or not Prefect issued it. That is the answer
# rather than a fault in it, because such a run is a key's format exactly and
# nothing in the text tells the two apart: sparing these would spare a real key
# written the same way. What is taken is a stretch of a value that was already
# opaque to a reader.

case:     the prefix inside a longer run of base64url
in:       payload=zzzzpnu_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzzzzz
out:      payload=zzzz«prefect-api-key»

case:     the prefix where a signature stands
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.zzzzpnu_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzzzzz
out:      eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.zzzz«prefect-api-key»

# A digest written behind the prefix. Hexadecimal digits are base62 and a digest
# carries nothing that ends a run, so a prefix and the forty characters of a
# SHA-1 are a key's format exactly, as a prefix and the sixty-four of a SHA-256
# are. Both are redacted. Declining them would mean declining every key Prefect
# happened to write in the digits alone, which is a whole credential against a
# cache key. What holds either side of it is the floor and the prefix: an MD5 is
# thirty-two characters, four short of a body, and a hyphen is no character a
# prefix carries.

case:     a sha1 behind the prefix
in:       pnu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «prefect-api-key»

case:     a sha256 in a cache key
in:       key: pnu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      key: «prefect-api-key»

case:     an md5 behind the prefix, four characters short of a body
in:       pnu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      pnu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a sha1 behind a hyphen rather than the prefix
in:       pnu-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      pnu-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

# And what this pattern leaves alone. The prefix is held to the case Prefect
# writes it in, to all four of its characters, and to naming one of the two
# kinds. A digest and a sentence hold no underscore where a prefix wants one, so
# they hold no position to be found at however long they run.

case:     an uppercase prefix
in:       PNU_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      PNU_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz

case:     a hyphen where the prefix carries an underscore
in:       pnu-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      pnu-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz

case:     a character naming no kind
in:       pna_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      pna_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz

case:     the opening and the underscore with no kind between them
in:       pn_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      pn_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz

case:     a body broken by a space
in:       pnu_0123456789abcdef ghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      pnu_0123456789abcdef ghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz

case:     a run of the right length opening with no prefix
in:       0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz

case:     a hexadecimal digest
in:       sha1=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      sha1=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     prose
in:       there is no credential in this sentence
out:      there is no credential in this sentence

# And a Prefect credential this pattern has nothing to say about. The key its
# first cloud issued is named by Prefect's CLI only to tell a caller which
# service the key was minted against, and what it names is three letters with no
# separator behind them. Three letters on their own open a candidate inside
# prose, and Prefect states no alphabet, no length and no character to close a
# prefix with, so there is nothing here to read a key by.

case:     a key of the format prefect cloud one issued
in:       PREFECT__CLOUD__API_KEY=pcu0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      PREFECT__CLOUD__API_KEY=pcu0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz

# Further text shapes a key is written in, and further adjacency the prefix and
# the run carry no boundary against.

case:     a key in a url query string
in:       https://api.prefect.cloud/api/accounts/0123/workspaces?api_key=pnu_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz&page=2
out:      https://api.prefect.cloud/api/accounts/0123/workspaces?api_key=«prefect-api-key»&page=2

case:     two keys in parentheses
in:       (pnu_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz, pnb_0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ)
out:      («prefect-api-key», «prefect-api-key»)

case:     a key followed by a carriage return and a newline
in:       PREFECT_API_KEY=pnb_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz\r\n
out:      PREFECT_API_KEY=«prefect-api-key»\r\n

case:     a key between tabs
in:       \tpnu_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz\t
out:      \t«prefect-api-key»\t

case:     a key between japanese
in:       日本語pnu_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz日本語
out:      日本語«prefect-api-key»日本語
